contracts.commit_point: conn.execute(sql, params).fetchall() inside ReadDb.query (db.py:185), where the supplied SQL is handed to SQLite; the read-only mode that defeats writes is registered earlier at sqlite3.connect in ReadDb.open (db.py:163-165).
contracts.declared_mechanism: ReadDb.open creates the connection with SQLite URI 'file:{path}?mode=ro' (db.py:163-165); that handle is the only database access wired to the agent (AgentDeps(db=db), __init__.py:158). ReadDb.query additionally appends 'LIMIT MAX_QUERY_ROWS' (100, db.py:17) when the stripped, uppercased, semicolon-trimmed SQL lacks the literal 'LIMIT' (db.py:182-184) before handing the statement to conn.execute (db.py:185). sqlite3.DatabaseError raised for rejected statements is converted to ModelRetry in the tool (tools.py:138-139).
contracts.forbidden_condition: Agent-supplied SQL executed via db_query producing any write/DDL mutation of the trace database file (the strace-derived pike-agent-*.db) during an agent session.
pending_binding_information: First-phase wording placed the commit point at sqlite3.connect in ReadDb.open (db.py:163-165); the merged contract records connect-time mode=ro as guard registration and resolves the effect commit point to conn.execute at db.py:185 per the second-phase wording.
Confirm that AgentDeps.db is the only database handle reachable from registered tools in the full repository (supplied views show only ctx.deps.db.query for database access).
Confirm that chat() is the only entry point constructing the agent with a ReadDb-bound AgentDeps (only this wiring appears in the supplied views).
contracts.protected_operation: Execution of model-supplied SQL by the db_query tool, routed as ctx.deps.db.query(sql) onto the shared read-only ReadDb connection.
contracts.protected_resource: The trace SQLite database opened by ReadDb.open(db_path) in chat() and bound into AgentDeps.
contracts.protection_obligation: The agent-registered db_query tool must never modify the trace SQLite database: SQL supplied by the model is executed only through the ReadDb connection opened in SQLite read-only mode (mode=ro), with an automatic 100-row LIMIT safety net bounding unbounded reads, so any write/DDL statement supplied by the agent fails instead of mutating the trace database. (Merged first- and second-phase reviewer wording; both describe the same obligation.)
scope_limits: The read-only guard covers only SQL executed through the ReadDb connection bound into AgentDeps; WriteDb (db.py:74-136) is a separate writable handle and the supplied views show no agent-reachable path to it.
The automatic LIMIT injection bounds result size only; it is skipped whenever the literal 'LIMIT' appears anywhere in the stripped, uppercased SQL (db.py:182-184) and is not itself a write guard.
How SQLite enforces mode=ro for specific statement forms, and whether the LIMIT substring check can be evaded, are runtime-behavior questions not decided from source.
Only the supplied line-numbered views were used; repository enumeration is incomplete, so other entry points or database handles outside these views are out of scope.

missing_information: No supplied view shows additional callers of ReadDb.query or other statements executed on the read-only connection during an agent session beyond ReadDb.schema() (db.py:173-178) and the db_query tool path, so completeness of the mode=ro guard across all agent-session database access cannot be confirmed from these views alone.

Behavior labels and runtime traces are unavailable per the stated scope, so the actual runtime failure mode of write/DDL statements under the mode=ro connection is not established by the supplied source.
Whether any other component mutates the trace database file (e.g., an out-of-process writer) during an agent session is not determinable from the supplied views.
